title: Will at least one additional U.S. state enact a cage-free egg requirement before July 2027?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, a U.S. state without an existing cage-free law in effect as of September 1, 2026, enacts a new cage-free requirement.

A cage-free requirement is a law or rule that either bans the use of cages for in-state hens or bans the sale of eggs from non-cage-free hens.
fine_print:
To qualify, a cage-free requirement may be enacted by the state legislature, passed by a ballot measure, or implemented via state administrative action. The requirement need not come into effect before January 1, 2027.

If a state legislature passes a cage-free requirement, that will suffice for this question to resolve as Yes, regardless of the action or inaction of the state's governor.

States with cage-free requirement on the books as of September 15, 2026 are Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, and Washington.
background:
Over the past century, the global population of egg-laying hens came to be largely contained in [battery cages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_cage). Such cages came to prominence because of the economic advantages they offer, but in more recent years, concerns have been raised by animal-welfare advocates that the use of cages causes excessive suffering. Consequently, battery cages have been banned in the European Union since 2012, and they are also banned in Bhutan, Norway, and Switzerland.

Within the United States, [various states](https://www.wherefoodcomesfrom.com/post/what-does-cage-free-eggs-mean) have [passed laws](https://www.aspca.org/improving-laws-animals/public-policy/farm-animal-confinement-bans) either requiring laying hens within the state to be cage-free or requiring eggs sold within the state to be from cage-free hens. States with laws that are either currently implemented or being phased in include Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, and Washington.
